citation.source: USDA FoodData Central (fdc.nal.usda.gov), raw whole egg — cracking doesn't change composition, only physical form, so egg.json's citation applies unchanged

Derived as the complement of egg_shell.json's own cited 10-12% shell fraction (1 - shell), not an independently sourced figure — CRACK spawns exactly egg_shell + egg_cracked (data/actions/crack.json's byproductsByAction), the yolk+white kept together rather than split, so this entity's mass is definitionally 'whatever the shell isn't.'
citation.note: Same confidence tier as egg_shell.json's own figure, since this number is entirely derived from it — see that file for the actual source discussion.

metadata.notes: Yolk and white opened out of the shell but deliberately NOT split apart — the entry point for scrambled eggs and the plain/French omelette (tortilla francesa), as opposed to egg_yolk/egg_white (data/entities/egg_yolk.json, egg_white.json) which come from SEPARATE. FRY on this entity ('fried', undisturbed sheet) reads as an omelette; SCRAMBLE ('scrambled', stirred curds) is the other outcome of the same pan+oil setup. isBeatable/BEAT (bowl, not mixer — data/actions/beat.json) replaced an earlier isBlendable/MIX wiring: MIX had no way to express 'a little vs. a lot', while BEAT's 'intensity' parameter (lightly_beaten/beaten/well_beaten) does, and a bowl-and-fork is the actual tool for this, not an electric mixer. Entirely optional and reachable from 'raw' either way — FRY/SCRAMBLE don't require a prior BEAT.
metadata.haccpNote: Carries the same egg_cooking CCP (data/ccps/egg_cooking.json) as the whole egg, on FRY/SCRAMBLE specifically — cracking and combining yolk/white is, if anything, a slightly *higher*-risk step than an intact shell egg (more surface exposed, potential pooling if multiple eggs are cracked together), which is exactly the FDA Food Code's own reasoning for treating broken/combined eggs 'for immediate service' under the same strict time-temperature standard as pooled eggs generally.
metadata.flipNote: isFlippable added for the plain/French omelette case (FLIP an already-frying egg_cracked to cook its second side) — cheap, directly reuses data/actions/flip.json as-is, no new machinery needed beyond what tortilla_mixture.json already required.
metadata.combineNote: isCombinableAddition: the secondary instance data/actions/combine.json consumes (poured over already-fried potato — see potato.json's combineNote). CLOSED 2026-08-17, a self-authored common-sense audit (not from an external document, LEARNINGS_PROCESS.md this date) — this note used to claim no statePrerequisite could enforce 'must be beaten first' because engine.ts's statePrerequisites only supported one exact required state string; that claim was already STALE by the time it was checked (array-valued OR-logic entries, e.g. potato.json's cut: ['washed','peeled'], have existed since 2026-08-15 — see engine.ts's own checkStatePrerequisite doc comment). More importantly, before this fix engine.ts's applyAction never checked ANY statePrerequisite on a SECONDARY instance at all (only the primary target) — a raw, never-beaten egg_cracked could be accepted as COMBINE's secondary. statePrerequisites.combine now requires ['beaten','well_beaten'] — the two intensities this repo's own real tortilla recipes actually use (tortilla-de-patatas.json: 'beaten'; tortilla-de-betanzos.json: 'well_beaten'); 'lightly_beaten' deliberately excluded despite this note's own prior speculation that it 'should' count — no real recipe or citation supports it, and an under-mixed egg (yolks/whites not fully incorporated) is a real, plausible failure mode for a tortilla that needs to hold together as one sheet, not obviously fine. Same fix, same reasoning, applied to combine_con_cebolla below.
metadata.combineConCebollaNote: Added 2026-08-17, same fix and same statePrerequisites.combine_con_cebolla: ['beaten','well_beaten'] as combineNote above — this entity is also the secondary instance of data/actions/combine_con_cebolla.json (see potato_onion_mixture.json's own metadata for that action's target side). Proven end-to-end via data/recipes/tortilla-de-patatas-con-cebolla.json (still simulates correctly — 'beaten' satisfies the new requirement) and scripts/physical-feasibility-rules-as-a-robot.ts (a never-beaten egg_cracked is now correctly rejected as this action's secondary).
metadata.seasoningNote: pepper/chili added 2026-08-13 alongside salt — see potato.json's identical seasoningNote. acid added 2026-08-15, same shape, same discipline.
metadata.invalidTransitionsNote: Closed 2026-08-15, ROADMAP.md Phase 4 — once fried or scrambled, cannot revert to raw or any beaten intensity: you cannot un-cook a set curd back into liquid egg. Deliberately does NOT forbid fried <-> scrambled cross-transitions in either direction — unlike un-cooking, nothing here asserts that's physically impossible (just an unusual thing to do), so it's left unenforced rather than guessed at.
metadata.rawContaminationRiskNote: Added 2026-08-16, mirroring egg.json's identical note/mechanism (src/tool-hygiene.ts). Every pre-fried/pre-scrambled state ('raw' through 'well_beaten') carries the risk — beating doesn't cook the egg, only fried/scrambled do, matching invalidTransitionsNote above's own 'cannot un-cook a set curd' reasoning applied to the opposite direction (nothing UP TO frying/scrambling has been heat-treated either).
metadata.foldNote: isFoldable + statePrerequisites.fold: 'fried' — the classical French omelette's rolled/folded shape, applied AFTER frying (data/actions/fold.json), not before. The Spanish tortilla francesa reading of this same entity (FRY, agitation: undisturbed, fully_set) simply never calls FOLD — both are equally valid, equally supported outcomes of the same starting entity; which one a request means is resolved upstream, not by this schema. See fry.json's internalTextureNote and data/recipes/tortilla-francesa.json / french-omelette.json.
